title: M0: Spike: ground truth for the DAW set format (.als) from sets the DAW saved
description:
## Purpose

Answer, with real files, what a DAW set has to contain before any spec or product code is written. The set format (`.als`, gzipped XML) is undocumented; every later milestone depends on its exact element names, id rules, units and ranges. This is a throwaway spike: it leaves a design note and reference fixtures, never product code.

## Questions the spike answers

1. The smallest set skeleton the target DAW version(s) open without complaint, and which version header (major/minor, creator) to write so both the current and the previous major version open it.
2. How ids work: per-element `Id`, pointee ids, the set-wide next-pointee counter; what must be unique.
3. An arrangement audio clip: position (beats), loop/start/end, warp on/off, warp markers (seconds ↔ beats), warp mode values, transpose (semitones), detune (cents), clip gain (units, range), reverse, and how a sample file is referenced (relative vs absolute path, the collected `Samples/Imported/` layout).
4. Set-level: tempo, time signature, loop brace, locators, the set's scale/key (if the version has one).
5. Mixer: group tracks (membership, nesting), return tracks, sends (units), track volume and pan (units, ranges), routing strings for a compressor sidechain.
6. Stock devices matching each Apricity effect (EQ Eight, Compressor, Limiter, Saturator, Redux, Gate, Utility, Reverb, Delay, Auto Filter): parameter names, units (real vs normalized) and ranges.
7. Automation envelopes: how an envelope points at a parameter, breakpoint format, step vs ramp.
8. Approach: template-and-patch (device XML captured from real sets) vs generating every element; decided by a hand-built proof set.

## Artifacts

- `design/daw-set.md`: format notes, the full Apricity → set mapping table, parameter unit conversions, decisions, remaining unknowns.
- Reference sets saved by the DAW in `crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/` (no audio; the audio they point to is a tiny synthetic WAV regenerated by a script).

## Out of scope

Product code, specs, CLI.

## Definition of Done

- Every question above answered in `design/daw-set.md`, or listed there as an open question for the owner.
- Reference sets committed; `git ls-files '*.wav' '*.aif*'` shows no audio.
- A hand-built proof set (from `apricity compile examples/march-blues.apr` output) opened in the DAW by the owner and played in time; result recorded as a comment here.
- Of the repo's feature checklist, only design note (6) and fixtures (5) apply; behavior specs, CLI, schema, docs and release do not (a spike ships no behavior).

## Dependencies

Blocks M1 to M5. Its findings on `.alc`/`.adg` XML are useful to apricitus-5562e0 and apricitus-d7746d.

comments.text:
## Where reference files come from (decided 2026-09-26, corrected)

Checked: the DAW is not installed on the owner's development Mac, and neither the persistent library (~5,500 files) nor the production bucket holds any `.als`, `.alc`, `.adg` or `.asd`. The owner does hold a paid Studio licence, installed on the studio machine. So:

1. **Reference files come from the owner's licensed install.** Its bundled Core Library ships thousands of `.adg`/`.alc` files and `.asd` sidecars beside its sample WAVs, and the owner's own sets supply `.als`. The spike's first task is a short list of exact paths and files to copy from the studio machine into a fixtures folder here (record each file's origin; never commit audio). Public git repositories are a supplement for older-version examples only.
2. **Test material.** Every test and conformance check runs against samples and manifests from the production library (sync it down read-only; never push). Pick a fixed, named handful for determinism.
3. **Acceptance.** Opening an export in the DAW happens on the studio machine, or on this Mac if the owner installs the licensed copy here. Acceptance tasks stay blocked, not skipped, until then; the machine-checkable conformance tests are the gate.

comments.text: **Not blocked on the DAW (owner, 2026-09-26).** The owner will install the licensed copy on this Mac, but said not to wait for it. Start now: gather reference files from public git repositories and the vendor's published format documentation, write the design note and conformance tests against them, and mark every finding that rests on a public file as *provisional*. When the local install appears, re-run the spike's checks against files from its library and the owner's sets, and update the note. Only the final acceptance tasks (opening an export in the DAW) wait on the install.

comments.text:
## Spike summary (2026-09-26)

**Answered** in design/daw-set.md with evidence from DAW-saved 12.x sets (12.0b16 to 12.4.5b10): the skeleton and header rules; the id rules (one set-wide pointee space below NextPointeeId, everything else list-local, track ids for routing); the full arrangement AudioClip (beats vs seconds, warp markers plus the trailing 1/32-beat marker, WarpMode 0-6, PitchCoarse/PitchFine, SampleVolume linear, FileRef RelativePathType 0/1/3/5/6/7, no reverse flag in 12); tempo and time signature (Manual plus the sentinel envelope, id = 99*log2(den)+num-1); loop brace, locators and scale; mixer units (volume and send linear gain, pan -1..1, groups, returns, sidechain AudioIn/Track.N/PostFxOut); device parameters for EQ Eight, Compressor, Limiter, Saturator, Utility, Reverb, Delay and Auto Filter; the automation envelope format. It also has a Mermaid tree, the Apricity to set mapping table, 13 Decisions (template-and-patch chosen) and 4 owner questions (copied to apricitus-6edba8).

**Provisional** (public or older files only): the exact header to write, clip gain max (+24 dB), clip fade units, collected-name clashes, the scale index table beyond Minor, nested groups in 12, Gate (11.0.12) and Redux (GPL dataset) XML, the EQ Eight band Mode order, Saturator Type order, Reverb Dry/Wet element, Auto Filter cutoff units, pan law, envelope interpolation domain, OriginalCrc 0 accepted.

**Waits on the DAW**: the owner's five reference sets (apricitus-6f10c9) and opening and listening to the proof set (apricitus-d6e7f5, built at renders/daw-proof/, deterministic). Both have click-by-click steps in the note. The 'Re-check when the licensed install arrives' list gives exact library paths.

**Files created**: design/daw-set.md; crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/reference/set/{README.md, public-12.3.7-minimal.als, public-12.2.1-techno.als, public-12.2-broom-bap.als} (MIT, unmodified); scripts/daw-reference-audio.py. Git-ignored outputs: renders/daw-reference/, renders/daw-proof/. Note: the sidecars spike added a second WAV generator (scripts/daw-fixture-audio.py); keep one.
